traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements for 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG are implemented and verified: - Core Functionality & Presets (REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG): src/index.ts exposes `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` as ESLint v9 flat-config arrays containing a rules severity map; tests show they enable the traceability rules when spread after a plugins registration object. - Quality Standards & Integration: Configuration uses ESLint v9 flat config patterns (FlatESLint overrideConfig arrays) and is demonstrated in user-docs for JS/TS/mixed projects, aligning with ESLint 9 best practices and integrating cleanly with existing configs. - Customization & Rule Options (REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, REQ-RULE-OPTIONS): valid-story-reference and require-story-annotation define JSON-schema-like meta.schema objects with documented properties (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension, scope, exportPriority) and disallow unknown options. - Config Validation & Error Handling (REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION): Misconfigured options cause ESLint to throw informative errors that reference the rule id, offending key, and type expectations, fulfilling the error-handling acceptance criterion. - Documentation & User Experience (REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION and doc-related acceptance criteria): The ESLint 9 Setup Guide and README show clear, concrete configuration examples, including how to spread `traceability.configs.recommended/strict` into user flat configs for common project types, with troubleshooting guidance. Given the concrete implementation and the passing, story-specific tests, this story is fully implemented and working as specified.
